City-traffic-M Road Volume with bdynets

  • 2 Read the supplied data

  • 5 Results
  • 6 Export the results

City Traffic Benchmarks v4 estimates five-minute road volume in Yekaterinburg from vehicle GPS observations. This example prepares road volume for 720 roads from the original-format Parquet records for 18 October 2024. The example prepares all 96 quarter-hours and traces one road from the source observations to a static map. The default map shows 08:00.

1 Set up the example

Start a fresh interactive R session in this example directory and run the visible R blocks in order. The setup loads the installed bdynets package and the example’s preparation functions. The Parquet step calls Python 3 with NumPy, pandas and PyArrow installed.

prepare.R contains this case’s conversion functions.

The expandable code blocks in the following steps show the definitions from the same scripts used by this report. The regular R blocks load those scripts, call the functions in order and show the resulting data. The Parquet reader is read_parquet.py. The local scripts/prepare-input.R aligns the road and time tables and writes the prepared RDS files. scripts/street-context.R reads the local background, and scripts/report-export.R saves the prepared data and static maps when export is requested.

library(bdynets)
source("scripts/prepare-input.R")
source("prepare.R")
source("scripts/report-export.R")
source("scripts/street-context.R")

if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("metropolis-traffic-report.Rmd")$params
}

The prepared input guide describes the final drawing object. For other source data, choose the fields, time intervals and conversion rules that fit that data.

2 Read the supplied data

Start with the two files in data/raw/. The static Parquet contains the source road attributes and coordinates. The volume Parquet contains all 288 five-minute timestamps from 18 October 2024 and retains the original volume columns. The source clock has no declared timezone. The supplied-file manifest describes these inputs. The upstream register records provenance, including the upstream volume file before the daily sample was made.

The supplied road list is the fixed 720-road selection carried over from the original Yekaterinburg case. It contains one road_id per row. Each ID gives a zero-based row in the static file and the suffix of its node_<id> column in the volume file.

In the call below, day = "2024-10-18" is the date expected in the supplied file. The reader checks that the full set of 288 timestamps matches it.

read_metropolis_raw() reads the chosen road columns and their matching static rows from the bundled Parquets through read_parquet.py. The actual dimensions and the records for the first road at 08:00 through 08:10 appear below. The nine source attributes shown here are the fields used by the conversion.

Python code that reads the Parquet columns, joins road IDs and calculates quarter-hour volumes 
"""Read the supplied day of five-minute volumes and the corresponding static roads.

Arguments: raw directory, road-ID CSV, output JSON, YYYY-MM-DD.
The caller supplies a temporary destination; this program never updates its inputs.
"""
import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq


def read_source_clock(volume_file, day):
    field_type = volume_file.schema_arrow.field('timestamp').type
    if getattr(field_type, 'tz', None) is not None:
        raise ValueError('This source reader expects timezone-unspecified release clocks.')
    raw = volume_file.read(columns=['timestamp']).column('timestamp').to_numpy()
    clock = raw.astype('datetime64[s]')
    if np.any(np.isnat(clock)) or np.any(raw != clock):
        raise ValueError('Volume clocks contain missing times or unsupported fractional seconds.')
    start = np.datetime64(day, 'D').astype('datetime64[s]')
    if not np.array_equal(clock, start + np.arange(288) * np.timedelta64(300, 's')):
        raise ValueError(f'The supplied day {day} needs 288 consecutive five-minute timestamps from midnight.')

    return clock


def read_native(directory, identifiers, day):
    paths = {name: directory / ('city-traffic-M-raw-' + name + '.parquet')
             for name in ('static-features', 'volume')}
    files = {key: pq.ParquetFile(path) for key, path in paths.items()}
    ids = [int(value) for value in identifiers]
    if not ids or len(set(ids)) != len(ids) or min(ids) < 0:
        raise ValueError('Road IDs must be distinct zero-based static-row identifiers.')
    static_fields = ['x_coordinate_start', 'y_coordinate_start', 'x_coordinate_end',
                     'y_coordinate_end', 'length', 'region_id', 'category', 'edge_type', 'speed_limit']
    static = files['static-features'].read(columns=static_fields).take(ids).to_pydict()
    volume_file = files['volume']
    day_clock = read_source_clock(volume_file, day)

    native = []
    for offset in range(0, len(ids), 48):
        columns = ['node_' + str(i) for i in ids[offset:offset + 48]]
        table = volume_file.read(columns=columns)
        for column in columns:
            values = table.column(column).to_numpy().astype(float)
            if np.any(~np.isfinite(values) | (values < 0)):
                raise ValueError(f'{column} has missing, infinite or negative volume on {day}.')
            native.append(values.tolist())
    for name in static:
        static[name] = [None if x is None else float(x) for x in static[name]]
    facts = {key: {'file': paths[key].name, 'bytes': paths[key].stat().st_size,
                  'rows': file.metadata.num_rows, 'columns': file.metadata.num_columns}
             for key, file in files.items()}
    data = pd.DataFrame(np.asarray(native, dtype=float).T, index=pd.to_datetime(day_clock))
    volume = data.resample('15min').mean().to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return {
        'schema': 'metropolis-flow-native-v1', 'ids': identifiers, 'static': static,
        'times': data.index.to_numpy(dtype='datetime64[s]').astype('int64').tolist(),
        'volume': native, 'source_files': facts,
        'clock': 'Source wall clock. No timezone is declared in the Parquets.',
        'source_summaries': {'flow': [round(float(row.mean()), 2) for row in volume]},
        'frame_values': {'volume': volume.T.tolist()},
        'summary_definition': 'Fifteen-minute means, then means across the selected roads before road-level rounding.'
    }


if __name__ == '__main__':
    directory, ids_file, destination, day = sys.argv[1:]
    with open(ids_file, encoding='utf-8', newline='') as handle:
        identifiers = [row['road_id'] for row in csv.DictReader(handle)]
    result = read_native(Path(directory), identifiers, day)
    with open(destination, 'x', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
        json.dump(result, handle, allow_nan=False, separators=(',', ':'))
R code that runs the Parquet reader and loads its temporary JSON 
read_metropolis_raw <- function(base, raw_dir, selection_file = file.path(base, 'data', 'selected-roads.csv'),
                                python = 'python3', day = '2024-10-18') {
  required <- c(metropolis_raw_files(raw_dir), selection_file)
  if (any(!file.exists(required)))
    stop('Missing original Parquet input or road register: ',
         paste(basename(required[!file.exists(required)]), collapse = ', '))
  path <- tempfile('metropolis-native-', fileext = '.json')
  diagnostic <- tempfile('parquet-reader-', fileext = '.log')
  on.exit(unlink(c(path, diagnostic)), add = TRUE)
  arguments <- c(file.path(base, 'read_parquet.py'), raw_dir, selection_file, path, day)
  status <- system2(python, shQuote(arguments), stderr = diagnostic)
  if (status != 0L) {
    lines <- readLines(diagnostic, warn = FALSE)
    detail <- grep('^(ValueError|ModuleNotFoundError|ImportError|KeyError|IndexError):', lines, value = TRUE)
    stop('The source Parquet reader failed. ',
         if (length(detail)) tail(detail, 1) else 'Check original fields and Python, NumPy, pandas and PyArrow.')
  }
  native <- jsonlite::read_json(path, simplifyVector = TRUE)
  native$static <- as.data.frame(native$static)
  native$times <- as.numeric(native$times)
  native
}

3 Prepare the drawing input

3.1 Inspect the native observations

read_metropolis_raw() passes the Parquet directory, road-ID CSV and date to read_parquet.py. The Python reader uses every timestamp in the supplied volume file and matches each road ID to its static row and volume column. It averages each set of three five-minute readings into an unrounded quarter-hour volume, then takes the mean across roads and rounds that mean to two decimals. The reader hands these results and the original five-minute values to R as temporary JSON. R reads that file into day_source and removes the temporary file.

The list contains the 720 road IDs and their static fields, the source times in seconds, and a volume matrix with one row per road and one column per original five-minute timestamp. The next step saves this list as source.rds.

print(data.frame(
  roads = nrow(day_source$volume),
  original_timestamps = ncol(day_source$volume)
), row.names = FALSE)
##  roads original_timestamps
##    720                 288

3.2 Prepare the road tables and save input.rds

Preparation takes the mean of three five-minute volume observations per quarter-hour. Each selected road needs a complete day of observations, including recorded zeros. The road ID links each volume to its geometry, and time gives the start of each quarter-hour.

Table How it is built
roads Start and end coordinates form the directed line in longitude and latitude. Road attributes come from the matching static row. The speed-limit field is a road attribute.
flow Quarter-hour volume is rounded to two decimals.
trends The quarter-hour mean across roads uses unrounded road volumes. The final mean is rounded to two decimals.

The conversion retains the source volume scale. metropolis_input() uses the computed quarter-hour volumes and preserves the counts of native observations.

Code that builds the road, quarter-hour Flow and trend tables 
metropolis_bins <- function(values, clock, prepared_values) {
  if (!is.matrix(values) || !nrow(values) || ncol(values) != length(clock) ||
      !is.numeric(clock) || any(!is.finite(clock)))
    stop('Native observations need a road-by-time matrix and complete source times.')
  if (length(clock) != 288L || clock[1] %% 86400 || any(diff(clock) != 300))
    stop('The source day must contain 288 consecutive five-minute slots beginning at midnight.')
  if (any(!is.finite(values) | values < 0))
    stop('The selected roads need complete finite, nonnegative native volume.')

  starts <- seq.int(1L, ncol(values), 3L)
  frame_dims <- c(nrow(values), length(starts))
  if (!identical(dim(prepared_values), frame_dims) || any(!is.finite(prepared_values) | prepared_values < 0))
    stop('Prepared quarter-hour volume must be finite, nonnegative and aligned to the source roads and times.')
  frame_names <- list(rownames(values), NULL)
  dimnames(prepared_values) <- frame_names
  status <- matrix(as.raw(ifelse(values == 0, 2L, 1L)), nrow(values), ncol(values),
                   dimnames = frame_names)
  list(values = prepared_values, times = clock[starts],
       coverage = list(native_times = clock, native_status = status,
                       frame_observed_n = matrix(3L, frame_dims[1], frame_dims[2], dimnames = frame_names)))
}

metropolis_input <- function(native) {
  if (!identical(native$schema, 'metropolis-flow-native-v1'))
    stop('Expected original five-minute volume and static road attributes.')
  ids <- as.character(native$ids)
  static <- native$static
  if (!length(ids) || anyNA(ids) || any(!nzchar(ids)) || anyDuplicated(ids) ||
      nrow(static) != length(ids) || nrow(native$volume) != length(ids))
    stop('Road IDs, original attributes and volume rows do not align.')
  rownames(native$volume) <- ids
  volume <- metropolis_bins(native$volume, native$times, native$frame_values$volume)
  roads <- data.frame(id = as.integer(ids), length = round(static$length, 1))
  if (all(c('region_id', 'category', 'edge_type', 'speed_limit') %in% names(static))) {
    code <- as.integer(static$speed_limit)
    code[is.na(code)] <- 0L
    limits <- c(NA, 5, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 110)
    if (any(!code %in% 0:11)) stop('Unknown source speed-limit code.')
    roads$source_region <- as.integer(static$region_id)
    roads$category <- as.integer(static$category)
    roads$edgeType <- as.integer(static$edge_type)
    roads$speedLimitCode <- code
    roads$speedLimit <- ifelse(code == 0, 'unknown', paste(limits[code + 1L], 'km/h'))
  }
  roads$road_id <- ids
  roads$geometry <- lapply(seq_along(ids), function(i) rbind(
    c(round(static$x_coordinate_start[i], 6), round(static$y_coordinate_start[i], 6)),
    c(round(static$x_coordinate_end[i], 6), round(static$y_coordinate_end[i], 6))))
  times <- volume$times
  flow <- data.frame(road_id = rep(ids, length(times)), time = rep(times, each = length(ids)),
                     flow = as.vector(round(volume$values, 2)))
  means <- native$source_summaries$flow
  if (length(means) != length(times) || any(!is.finite(means)))
    stop('Source volume summaries must match the selected full-day frame domain.')
  trends <- data.frame(time = times, metric = 'flow', value = as.numeric(means),
                       definition = 'Mean unrounded frame volume across the selected source roads.', label = 'flow')
  list(crs = 'EPSG:4326', roads = roads, flow = flow, trends = trends,
       title = 'City-traffic-M traffic volume', time_label_format = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M',
       times = times, interval_seconds = rep(900, length(times)), unit = 'source volume',
       provenance = list(
         source_dataset = 'mightyneghbor/city-traffic-benchmarks v4',
         clock = 'Source wall clock; timezone is unspecified.',
         selection = sprintf('The supplied %d-road register and %s source date.',
                             length(ids), format(as.POSIXct(native$times[1L], origin = '1970-01-01', tz = 'UTC'),
                                                 '%Y-%m-%d', tz = 'UTC')),
         source_files = native$source_files[c('static-features', 'volume')],
         source_summary_definition = native$summary_definition,
         native_coverage = list(status_codes = c(observed_nonzero = 1L, observed_zero = 2L),
                                volume = volume$coverage)),
       metric_info = list(flow = list(unit = 'source volume',
         definition = 'Mean of the three native five-minute volume values in each quarter hour.')))
}
Code that passes the native object and road tables to the writer 
write_metropolis_prepared <- function(native, output_dir, raw_dir, selection_file) {
  meanings <- c(id = 'Zero-based static Parquet row ID.',
                length = 'Source road length in metres, rounded to one decimal.',
                source_region = 'Source region_id category.', category = 'Source category code.',
                edgeType = 'Source edge_type code.', speedLimitCode = 'Source speed_limit category.',
                speedLimit = 'Source speed-limit category decoded using the source map lookup.')
  dictionary <- rbind(data.frame(table = 'roads', field = names(meanings), meaning = unname(meanings)),
    data.frame(table = 'trends', field = c('definition', 'label'),
               meaning = c('Definition of this derived source summary.', 'Display label for the summary metric.')))
  write_traffic_input(metropolis_input(native), output_dir,
    source_files = c(metropolis_raw_files(raw_dir), selection_file),
    native = native, dictionary = dictionary)
}
Code that aligns the drawing matrix and writes all three RDS files 
.prep_road_frames <- function(input) {
  if (!is.list(input) || is.null(names(input)) || anyDuplicated(names(input)))
    stop('Supply a uniquely named list of prepared tables.', call. = FALSE)
  if (any(c('nodes', 'flows', 'od', 'speed') %in% names(input)))
    stop('Flow, Speed and OD inputs are separate formats.', call. = FALSE)
  schema <- input[['schema']]
  if (!is.null(schema) && !identical(schema, 'bdynets-flow-input-v1'))
    stop('Unsupported Flow input schema.', call. = FALSE)
  roads <- input[['roads']]
  observations <- input[['flow']]
  if (!is.data.frame(roads) || !all(c('road_id', 'geometry') %in% names(roads)) ||
      !is.data.frame(observations) || !all(c('road_id', 'time', 'flow') %in% names(observations)))
    stop('Flow tables require roads(road_id, geometry) and flow(road_id, time, flow).', call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(roads$road_id) || !is.character(observations$road_id))
    stop('Road IDs must be character in both Flow tables.', call. = FALSE)
  if (is.null(input[['unit']])) stop('Supply the Flow unit.', call. = FALSE)
  input[['schema']] <- NULL
  if (any(!names(input) %in% names(formals(traffic_data))))
    stop('Unknown Flow input fields.', call. = FALSE)
  frames <- do.call(traffic_data, input)
  frames$input_type <- 'flow'
  frames
}

write_traffic_input <- function(input,output_dir,source_files=character(),native=NULL,dictionary=NULL) {
  target<-.prep_destination(output_dir,source_files)
  parent<-dirname(target);dir.create(parent,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
  lock<-paste0(target,'.preparation-lock')
  if(!dir.create(lock,showWarnings=FALSE))stop('Another preparation is using this output directory.',call.=FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(lock,recursive=TRUE,expand=FALSE),add=TRUE)
  .prep_destination(output_dir,source_files)
  stage<-tempfile('prepared-data-',tmpdir=parent)
  if(!dir.create(stage))stop('Cannot create preparation staging directory.',call.=FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(stage,recursive=TRUE,expand=FALSE),add=TRUE)
  info_before<-file.info(source_files)[,c('size','mtime'),drop=FALSE]
  identities<-.prep_sources(source_files)
  object<-input
  object$provenance$preparation_sources <- identities
  road_frames <- .prep_road_frames(object)
  object$schema <- 'bdynets-flow-input-v1'
  tables <- .prep_tables(object)
  dictionary <- .prep_dictionary(tables, object, dictionary)
  na_token<-'\\N'
  strings<-unlist(lapply(tables,function(t)unlist(lapply(t,function(x)if(is.character(x))x else character()),use.names=FALSE)),use.names=FALSE)
  while(na_token%in%strings)na_token<-paste0(na_token,'_')
  saveRDS(object,file.path(stage,'input.rds'),compress='xz',version=3)
  saveRDS(road_frames,file.path(stage,'flow-frames.rds'),compress='xz',version=3)
  if(!is.null(native))saveRDS(native,file.path(stage,'source.rds'),compress='xz',version=3)
  for(name in names(tables)) {
    tab<-as.data.frame(.prep_csv(tables[[name]]),stringsAsFactors=FALSE,optional=TRUE)
    utils::write.csv(tab,file.path(stage,paste0(name,'.csv')),row.names=FALSE,na=na_token,fileEncoding='UTF-8')
  }
  utils::write.csv(dictionary,file.path(stage,'data-dictionary.csv'),row.names=FALSE,na='')
  utils::write.csv(identities,file.path(stage,'source-files.csv'),row.names=FALSE)
  metadata<-object[setdiff(names(object),names(tables))]
  metadata$input_type <- 'flow'
  metadata$csv<-list(missing=na_token,timestamp='POSIXct times are Unix seconds; numeric times retain the declared source clock.',
                     identifiers='Read identifier fields as character.',data='input.rds preserves original types, geometry, timezones and nested provenance.')
  writeLines(jsonlite::toJSON(.tm_provenance_for_json(metadata),auto_unbox=TRUE,null='null',na='null',digits=NA,pretty=TRUE),file.path(stage,'metadata.json'),useBytes=TRUE)
  files<-sort(list.files(stage))
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(file=files,md5=unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(stage,files)))),file.path(stage,'checksums.csv'),row.names=FALSE)
  if(!identical(info_before,file.info(source_files)[,c('size','mtime'),drop=FALSE]))stop('A source changed during preparation.',call.=FALSE)
  .prep_destination(output_dir,source_files)
  if(!file.rename(stage,target))stop('Cannot publish the completed preparation.',call.=FALSE)
  invisible(file.path(target,'input.rds'))
}

3.3 From the road table to the exact drawing input

The preparation writer takes every frame start in input.rds in order and every entry in roads$road_id in road-table order. Each observation is placed at values[match(time, times), match(road_id, roads$road_id)]. The matrix starts with NA cells, so missing road–time observations stay missing and observed zeros remain zero. The resulting object also carries the ordered road geometries, frame widths, units and any prepared events. Preparation saves that object as flow-frames.rds. This is the standard drawing input. input.rds is the earlier table export for inspecting or reusing the conversion.

The worked road, 21263, has source volumes of 70, 72, and 65 in the three five-minute observations starting at 08:00. Their mean of 69.00 appears in the prepared flow table and in the road’s 08:00 matrix cell.

example_time <- as.numeric(worked_times[1L])
time_row <- match(example_time, day_view$times)
road_column <- match(example_road, day_view$roads$road_id)
source_row <- match(example_road, day_source$ids)
observation <- subset(day_input$flow, road_id == example_road & time == example_time)

data.frame(
  road_id = observation$road_id, time = observation$time,
  time_row = time_row, road_column = road_column,
  mean_of_source_observations = mean(day_source$volume[source_row, native_slots]),
  value_in_input_table = observation$flow,
  value_in_drawing_matrix = day_view$values[time_row, road_column]
)
##   road_id       time time_row road_column mean_of_source_observations
## 1   21263 1729238400       33           1                          69
##   value_in_input_table value_in_drawing_matrix
## 1                   69                      69
data.frame(frame_rows = nrow(day_view$values),
  road_columns = ncol(day_view$values), unit = day_view$unit)
##   frame_rows road_columns          unit
## 1         96          720 source volume

4 Draw the selected frame

The prepared input contains all 96 quarter-hours. Its numeric time keys preserve the source wall clock, and each frame begins at a quarter-hour. The map call selects one frame by its start time and draws the full prepared road extent. Its seven log1p colour classes are based on the complete series.

4.1 Load the offline background

Load the supplied OpenStreetMap background for the Yekaterinburg road extent. The GeoJSON was prepared from OpenFreeMap vector tiles. Its roads, water and place names provide context for the measured road layer.

street_paths <- "data/basemap-cache/yekaterinburg.geojson.gz"
basemap <- if (isTRUE(params$basemap)) read_case_streets(street_paths)
plot_time <- params$plot_time
plotted <- traffic_flow_map(
  flow_frames, time_label = plot_time, basemap = basemap,
  full_extent = TRUE, padding = 0.04
)

City-traffic-M road volume at the selected frame start.

5 Results

The curve summarises the same road values that the map draws, including recorded zeros. These road values are already rounded to two decimals. The separate trends table in input.rds rounds each mean after averaging the unrounded road values, so the two series can differ slightly. The dashed line marks the frame shown on the map.

trend <- traffic_trend(day_view)
plot(trend, metric = "mean", index = plotted$index,
     ylab = "Mean road volume (source units)")

6 Export the results

Preparation saves its working files in a temporary directory. The draw calls use the current R graphics device. When running the blocks with Rscript and no device open, R can create Rplots.pdf in the working directory. To regenerate the report HTML and keep the selected map and complete drawing data, run this command from the example directory:

Rscript run.R 08:00 --offline --export

Replace 08:00 with another prepared frame start to draw that frame. The default destination is a new output/ directory. To use a different new directory, add --output-dir NEW_DIRECTORY.

The command saves the selected map at output/maps/metropolis-flow.png. output/prepared-data/flow-frames.rds contains all prepared frames and can be passed to the same plotting function to draw another frame. The directory also contains source.rds and input.rds, which record intermediate preparation steps.
